text: In software development, Git branching is a powerful tool that helps teams work together without stepping on each other’s toes. Instead of everyone editing the same main version, each person or team can create a *feature branch*. This is a separate copy of the code where you can add new features or fix bugs safely. Once your work is finished, you can submit a *pull request*, which is a formal way to ask others to review your changes. After the review, the branch is *merged* back into the main code. This version control workflow keeps the main project stable and makes collaboration much cleaner and more organized.
